newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks seen rising, led by high-tech sector.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks seen rising, led by high-tech sector.

text.p: Tokyo stocks are likely to extend their gains on Tuesday, after climbing more than 300 points and breaking through 20,000 on the previous day, as investors' interest in high-technology shares is expected to remain strong, brokers said.
The market is also likely to be supported by hopes that pension funds will purchase stocks in the middle of this month, they said.
On Monday, the 225-share Nikkei average ended up 353.23 points or 1.78 percent at 20,228.72. Its September futures added 400 points to close at 20,240.
"With lingering fears over the credit risks of companies, investors are seeking issues backed by healthy assets and earnings," said Kenji Karikomi, deputy general manager at Daiwa Securities Co Ltd.

"Dealers who took profits in high-tech shares, especially semiconductors yesterday, are likely to hunt for the same issues again. The Nikkei 225 will likely try 20,500," said a broker at a medium-sized Japanese securities house.
Turnover was a modest 189 million shares at midday, against 211 million shares traded by midday on Monday.
Losers outnumbered gainers 534 to 445, while 245 issues were unchanged.
In other indices, the broader-based TOPIX index lost 2.44 points or 0.16 percent to end the morning session at 1,522.70. The Nikkei 300 average gave up 0.35 point or 0.12 percent to 296.08.
Sony's shares closed the morning session unchanged at 10,100 after earlier rising to an all-time high of 10,300 yen. The previous record of 10,100 yen was recorded on June 3.
Shares of Tokyo Electron hit a record high of 6,650 yen, renewing the record for the first time in 13 years. It ended the morning at 6,610 yen, up 80 yen from Monday's close.
"While firms seen with poor financial health were sold off, blue-chip issues were sought after, accelerating a polarisation of the market," said a trader at a major securities house.

In late morning, Japan's Transport Ministry announced that it will list 1.5 million state-owned shares of Central Japan Railway Co (JR Tokai) on October 8. Of the total 1.5 million shares, 700,000 shares will be auctioned and the rest will be sold in the market through a secondary offering, it said.
Analysts said the listing might hurt the market later this year by possibly causing a supply glut, especially if further sales of shares in formerly state-owned firms emerge.
Shares of Hokkaido Bank Ltd and Hokkaido Takushoku Bank Ltd dipped on news that their planned merger could be delayed.
Shares of Hokkaido Bank were down four yen at 140 yen at midday, while Hokkaido Takushoku was down one yen at 143 yen.
By sector, decliners were led by fisheries, pulp/paper, and mining. The major gainers were brokerages, gas, and trading houses. -- Hiroko Nakata, Tokyo Equities Desk +81-3-3432-8027
